questions.q: Which DMV reports real index fragmentation percentage and page count?
options: sys.dm_exec_sessions
sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats
sys.database_principals
sys.server_principals
questions.explain: sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats is the function used to measure fragmentation before deciding on a maintenance action.

questions.q: Per Microsoft's standard thresholds, what action is recommended for an index at 18% fragmentation?
options: Do nothing
REORGANIZE
REBUILD
DROP and recreate the table
questions.explain: 18% falls in the 5%–30% range, where REORGANIZE (lighter, always online) is the standard recommendation.

questions.q: What does ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD do to an index's statistics, as a side effect?
options: Leaves them completely untouched
Refreshes them but only with a small sampled scan
Refreshes them with a full scan
Deletes them, requiring a manual UPDATE STATISTICS afterward
questions.explain: REBUILD refreshes the index's statistics as a side effect, using a full scan rather than the default sampled scan REORGANIZE and manual UPDATE STATISTICS use.

questions.q: What does REORGANIZE offer that REBUILD does not, in terms of operational behavior?
options: It refreshes statistics with a full scan
It fully resolves fragmentation regardless of severity
It is always an online operation and can be stopped mid-way without losing progress
It requires Enterprise edition
questions.explain: REORGANIZE never takes a blocking schema modification lock and resumes gracefully if interrupted — REBUILD without ONLINE = ON blocks for its duration.

questions.q: Why does a real production index-maintenance job typically loop through sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats rather than hardcoding one ALTER INDEX statement per table?
options: Because sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats deletes fragmented indexes automatically
Because hardcoded statements are faster to execute
Because ALTER INDEX cannot be run more than once against the same index
Because fragmentation varies per index over time, so the threshold-based decision (do nothing / reorganize / rebuild) needs to be evaluated dynamically each run
questions.explain: Fragmentation changes over time and varies per index, so a real maintenance job evaluates the current fragmentation and applies the appropriate threshold-driven action dynamically, which is what Ola Hallengren's scripts (Lesson 38) do in a maintained, parameterized way.
